Hey Mel, thanks Lou for the tag. Usual disclaimer: I haven't seen your leg so I can't diagnose it over a forum. But what you're describing (stiff first thing, sore to squeeze a few cm up from the heel, warms up then aches that night, after a big jump in k's) sounds a lot like a classic mid-portion tendinopathy rather than a tear. Tendons don't love going from 30 to 48 in three weeks!

You don't need to stop completely, but the limping after your 6k says that's too much right now. Drop the k's back to whatever you can run without it flaring, keep it flat and easy, and leave out hills and speed for a bit.

Loading is the main treatment:
- Heel drops are fine, but heavy slow calf raises have better evidence these days. Go 3 secs up, 3 secs down, 3 sets of around 15, every second day. Add weight (backpack, then a machine) as it gets easy.
- On the bad days, do isometric holds instead. Hold halfway up on the sore leg for 30-45 secs, 4-5 times. That usually settles it down a bit.

As a rough guide to pain, up to 3/10 while you're loading or running is ok, as long as it's settled by the next morning and the morning stiffness isn't getting worse. If it's worse the next day, back off a notch.

I'd steer clear of hard stretching and cortisone injections near the Achilles. Stretching into the burn tends to irritate it more, and cortisone around the tendon can weaken it and raise the risk of it rupturing. Good news since you're not keen on a needle anyway!

Also worth knowing that some antibiotics, the fluoroquinolone group (cipro and similar), are linked to tendon problems. If you ever get prescribed one, mention your Achilles to the GP or pharmacist.

If it's not settling in 3-4 weeks, see a sports physio. There are plenty around your way in Bayswater, any of them will be able to help.

The urgent one: if you feel a sudden pop, it feels like someone kicked you in the back of the leg, or you suddenly can't push off on that foot, stop running and stop the calf work. Get it checked that same day at a GP or ED, because it could be a rupture and timing matters.

Good luck with the build to Rotto, you've got plenty of time to sort it before Feb.
